CakePHP and Slim apps to PHP 8.5#

This page covers the three framework hops for CakePHP and Slim apps: the commands, what each hop changes, and the MANUAL list each one prints. Before this: Hand-copied libraries to Composer. Next: Strict session IDs for raw PHP apps.

Booster 1.20 takes a CakePHP 4 app to CakePHP 5.4 and a Slim 3 app to Slim 4.15, and moves PHP to 8.5 around those steps. The frameworks hold PHP back: CakePHP 4.5 stops at PHP 8.3 and Slim 3.12 at 7.3, so the PHP hops wait for the framework hop that lets them go on. PHP 8.6 is out; Booster's 8.6 hops follow once CakePHP and Slim support it.

CakePHP and Slim are being phased out at WSU (D-124): these hops keep existing apps supported; new apps start on raw PHP or Laravel (Sourdough or WELD).

composer global require waynestate/booster:^1.20
booster detect --path=../my-app
booster plan   --path=../my-app --to-php 8.5
booster run    --path=../my-app --replay --to-php 8.5

detect names the framework and its major.minor (framework cakephp 4.5 or framework slim 3.12), read from composer.lock. plan puts the framework hops between the PHP hops, and run applies them one at a time, each gated by the app's tests and the replay. Pass --to-php 8.5 to both: it keeps the plan and the run on the same target. --to-cakephp and --to-slim pick the framework line (the newest by default; --to-cakephp 4 stops on 4.6).

Point Booster at the folder with composer.json. Plenty of Slim apps keep it under src/, next to the code, not at the repository root. Booster reads the framework from that file and refuses a hop without it, so give it that folder:

booster plan --path=../my-app/src --to-php 8.5

--replay matters here. The tests a CakePHP or Slim app ships with (often the skeleton's, or none) prove very little about a framework move, so the replay is the real gate for both frameworks. Run booster replay init --path=../my-app first and read the draft (see The replay gate). For Slim it lists the route calls it finds, as written: a route inside a group shows up without the group's prefix, so add the prefix by hand and keep at least one request per group, which is what catches a group that lost its prefix. CakePHP routes declared with connect() are not drafted, so check the draft against bin/cake routes and add the pages that matter.

What a CakePHP 4 app gets#

Two hops, cakephp-4-to-4.6 then cakephp-4.6-to-5, with the PHP hops between them:

  1. cakephp-4-to-4.6 runs CakePHP's own upgrade rules for 4.1 through 4.5 (cakephp/upgrade, in a container, over a copy of the app, so a rule set that fails halfway leaves the app as it was), then requires cakephp/cakephp ^4.6 and the matching versions of the CakePHP plugins the app already lists. It goes first, on the PHP the app runs today, when that is 7.4 or newer; an app below 7.4 gets the PHP hops to 7.4 first, then this one.
  2. PHP moves to 8.2, the first PHP CakePHP 5.4 runs on.
  3. cakephp-4.6-to-5 runs the 5.0 through 5.4 rules (with Chronos 3 and Migrations), renames .ctp templates to .php under templates/ and moves the locales, moves AuthComponent to the Authentication plugin, swaps the Oracle driver if the app has it, and requires CakePHP 5.4 with the plugins that match.
  4. PHP moves on to 8.5.

A CakePHP 4.3 app on PHP 8.1 therefore plans cakephp-4-to-4.6, php-81-to-82, cakephp-4.6-to-5, then php-82-to-83, php-83-to-84 and php-84-to-85. The same app on PHP 7.3 plans php-73-to-74 first, then cakephp-4-to-4.6, then the same course. Stop on 4.6 with --to-cakephp 4: it still runs on PHP 8.5, but 4.x is end of life, so treat it as a rest stop, not a home. A target PHP below 8.2 leaves the CakePHP 5 step out with a warning, --skip cakephp-4.6-to-5 leaves it out too, and the PHP hops then stay within what 4.6 runs on.

Fix deprecations first. Run your tests with error_reporting(E_ALL) on CakePHP 4.6 and fix every deprecation notice before the 5 step. A deprecation on 4.6 is CakePHP 5 knocking politely; on 5 it stops knocking. Booster tells you; it does not fix them for you.

The sign-in move. The 5 step moves the like-for-like AuthComponent calls ($this->Auth->user('x') reads the identity, setUser() becomes setIdentity(), logout() and allow() keep their names on $this->Authentication), swaps loadComponent('Auth') for loadComponent('Authentication.Authentication'), requires cakephp/authentication ^3.0, and wires src/Application.php: the provider interface, the plugin, the middleware after routing, and a service with the Session authenticator whose guests go to the old loginAction.

What Booster does not do (the MANUAL list). Each run prints these as MANUAL: lines, with the file and the count where there is one:

  • On the 4.6 step: the reminder to fix every deprecation with E_ALL before the 5 step.
  • On both steps: View::loadHelper() calls the rules could not type (it is addHelper() since 4.5).
  • Sign-in that is not a plain session: isAuthorized() (move it to Authorization plugin policies or plain controller code), and any Auth config the plugin has no like-for-like for (authenticate with a custom authenticator such as CAS, an SSO cookie or an LTI launch, authorize, loginRedirect, logoutRedirect, authError; loginAction is carried over as the redirect). Also an 'Auth' entry with config in a $components list, any other $this->Auth->...() call, what the action does with logout()'s return value (now the redirect URL or null), and allow() calls that passed one name or none, since allowUnauthenticated() takes an array.
  • src/Application.php that Booster could not wire: no such file or class, one that already provides an authentication service (check that it loads the Session authenticator), no bootstrap() or middleware(), no routing middleware, or no loginAction found (the redirect is the placeholder /login).
  • Code no rule moves: RequestHandlerComponent (declare viewClasses() instead), ->withType() calls, Cake\Mailer\Email (use Mailer), Cake\I18n\Time and the mutable Cake\I18n\Date (use DateTime or the immutable Date, and check code that changed a date in place), and any .ctp template left over.
  • cakedc/cakephp-oracle-driver has no CakePHP 5 release. The 5 step swaps it for ioigoume/cakephp5-oracle-driver and renames its namespace; check that it covers the Oracle calls your app makes.
  • App bugs the move exposes are reported, never fixed: the hop moves the framework, not the app's own logic.

What a Slim 3 app gets#

One hop, slim-3-to-4, at the lowest PHP Slim 4.15 runs on (7.4: first when the app is already there, else right after the PHP hop that lands on 7.4), then the PHP hops to 8.5. --to-slim 3.13 is refused: Booster moves Slim 3 apps to Slim 4.15.

  • new \Slim\App([...]) becomes LegacyApp::create([...]) over your existing Pimple container, which keeps every $container['x'], $c->x and $c->get('x') working, and LegacyApp::finish($app) goes in just before $app->run(). No PHP-DI rewrite. The three glue classes (LegacyContainer, LegacyDoublePass, LegacyApp) are written into a Legacy folder under the app's PSR-4 root, so they are your code from then on.
  • finish() adds what Slim 3 did by itself, from the same settings: displayErrorDetails goes to the error middleware, outputBuffering to the output-buffering middleware, addContentLengthHeader to the content-length middleware, routerCacheFile to the route cache. The routing middleware runs before your own, so the route is resolved before your middleware sees the request. Body parsing is added, because Slim 3 parsed JSON and XML itself.
  • Every add() middleware keeps its ($request, $response, $next) shape through the LegacyDoublePass adapter. Move each one to PSR-15 when you next touch it, and delete the adapter when nothing uses it.
  • Route groups: function () use ($app) becomes a callable that takes the group, so prefixes survive, and a route adder typed \Slim\App that a group calls is widened to take the group too.
  • $request->getAttribute('route') becomes RouteContext::fromRequest($request)->getRoute().
  • composer.json gets slim/slim ^4.15, pimple/pimple ^3 and slim/psr7 ^1.7, plus slim/twig-view ^3.4 and twig/twig ^3.8 when the app already lists them.

What Booster does not do (the MANUAL list). Each run prints these as MANUAL: lines, with the file and line:

  • Route exceptions now reach Slim's error middleware before your own PHP error or exception handler. Register your handler with the error middleware if you want the old page and logging. This line is always printed.
  • The errorHandler, phpErrorHandler, notFoundHandler and notAllowedHandler container keys (Slim 4 never reads them), settings Slim 4 has no equivalent for, and $settings->get('k'), now a plain array read.
  • pathFor(), urlFor() and relativePathFor() calls (build the URL with the route parser), and Twig templates that call path_for( or base_url( (Twig-View 3 has url_for).
  • getAttribute('routeInfo'), subRequest(), setArgument() calls to check, Slim\Http\Environment, the container's router, request, response and environment entries, and code in outer middleware that reads the route before routing ran.
  • A group callable that uses $this, or calls $app without use ($app), a route adder typed \Slim\App that was not widened, and middleware added by its container name.
  • LegacyApp::finish($app) where Booster could not place it, and a glue file that already exists and differs from the one the hop writes.

What has no hop yet#

CakePHP 3 and Slim 2 (and anything older): booster plan says Booster has no hop for them yet and keeps PHP where the framework still runs, instead of planning a break. Moving a CakePHP or Slim app to Laravel is coming next; nothing in this release does it.

See also: What a hop does, The replay gate, and every hop's notes in Hops.
